body.rationale: The governing IPS (config/ips.yaml) is still a draft, so I weight IPS compliance as provisional but still informative. My picks favour candidates that either pass the draft hard limits or sit close to them, and that rely on the covariance structure more than on return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding in §4.3. First choice is resampled_efficient_frontier. It passes every hard limit and is the most diversified of the compliant group (effective N 13.3). Its Sharpe is 0.41 and its backtest Sharpe 0.63. The CRO risk score is 0.44. Its flaws are a drawdown headroom under 1 point (-24.3% vs -25%) and a muddled description of the gamma tuning. Those are real but fixable and do not undermine the core construction. Second is black_litterman. It is IPS clean, has a backtest Sharpe of 0.70 and a max drawdown of -21.2%, which is the best among the compliant return-optimised group. Its intra-category reviewer verified the numbers, and the one technical error flagged concerns the explanation, not the weights. Third is pc_researcher. It has the best blend of Sharpe (0.51) and a modest drawdown (-10.9%), with a backtest Sharpe of 0.70. It breaches only volatility and tracking error, which are softer given the draft IPS. Reviewers noted the Sharpe floor inconsistency and the gap between narrative and output, so I place it below the clean passers. Fourth is tail_risk_parity. It is a different tail-aware approach from mine, it has a reasonable effective N of 6.0 and a low drawdown (-7.2%), and it uses downside risk rather than return forecasts. It breaches the return, volatility and tracking-error limits, so I rank it below the compliant candidates. Fifth is max_sharpe. It passes the IPS with the highest compliant Sharpe (0.46), but it holds 46% in us_value, driven by one judged CMA gap, as its reviewers noted. That fragility is why it comes last in my five. The first choice beats the fifth because resampling averages over estimation noise and is diffuse, so it avoids the single-gap concentration that makes max_sharpe fragile, while giving up little Sharpe. I flag market_cap_weight. It has the worst drawdown (-40.6%) and the highest CRO risk (0.80), it breaches the drawdown limit, and its ETF-AUM proxy was judged invalid by an intra-category reviewer as not a true capitalisation weighting. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier: its single-asset vertex is by design orthogonal to consensus and is useful as an ensemble diversifier, even though I do not rank it.
